outcome: No proof or disproof of the number-field Bombieri–Lang conjectures appeared in the window: the arithmetic statement is still open in every case I could find. The geometric (function-field, characteristic 0) analogue for projective varieties with finite maps to abelian varieties was claimed in full by Guoquan Gao (arXiv:2511.17010, first posted 21 Nov 2025 as 'A complete proof', retitled 'A counting argument' on 2 Mar 2026); no journal acceptance or independent check was found. The earlier Xie–Yuan results on the same geometric question were first posted in May and August 2023, before the window, and their main paper was published in Acta Mathematica in 2026.
problem_asks: The statement, unpacked: (a) the surface case: for a surface of general type defined over a number field, its rational points are not Zariski dense (the conjecture as Bombieri stated it for surfaces). (b) the same for algebraic varieties of arbitrary dimension: for a positive-dimensional variety of general type over a number field, the rational points are not Zariski dense (Lang's extension). (c) the density-refined form: there is a dense open U such that U has finitely many points over every finite extension of the base number field. (d) the field-extension clause: the same finiteness/non-density assertions for varieties of general type over fields that are finitely generated extensions of number fields (the strong form, read as fields finitely generated over Q). Reading note: the statement does not name the geometric (function-field over characteristic 0) version; I treat 'field extensions' as finitely generated extensions of number fields, which is the reading the Wikipedia article's strong form uses. The competing broader reading is recorded in competing_reading.

events.what_happened: Giulio Bresciani, 'On the Bombieri-Lang Conjecture over finitely generated fields', arXiv:2012.15765 (first submitted 31 Dec 2020). The abstract states that the strong Bombieri–Lang conjecture reduces to the case k = Q (unconditionally), and that assuming the geometric Lang conjecture the weak form also reduces to k = Q. Published as Algebra & Number Theory 16 (2022) 2409–2414 per the arXiv journal reference.
events.revisions: v2 5 Apr 2022, comment: 'Edited for clarity. Fixed a wrong notation in the proof of Theorem A that confused some readers'. Journal reference Alg. Number Th. 16 (2022) 2409–2414.
events.delivers: Reductions only. Unconditionally: the strong form over fields finitely generated over Q reduces to the base field Q. Conditionally on the geometric Lang conjecture: the weak form reduces to Q. No case of any form of the conjecture over Q or any number field is settled.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the surface and all-dimension weak forms over number fields, the refined form, and the strong form over Q itself.
events.time_since_posted: about 5 years 9 months as of 11 Oct 2026; pre-window, citing work not searched beyond this
events.direction: Reduces the arithmetic question to the base field Q. Neither proves nor disproves a case.

events.what_happened: Junyi Xie and Xinyi Yuan, 'Partial Heights and the Geometric Bombieri-Lang Conjecture', arXiv:2305.14789 v1 (24 May 2023). v2 (6 Aug 2023) is retitled 'Partial Heights, Entire Curves, and the Geometric Bombieri-Lang Conjecture'. Abstract as read in v2: they prove the geometric Bombieri–Lang conjecture for hyperbolic projective varieties with a finite morphism to an abelian variety over function fields of characteristic 0, by building an entire curve from a sequence of rational points via Brody's lemma; the approach is conditional on a non-degeneracy conjecture for partial heights. Later published in Acta Mathematica 236 (2026), 365–416, DOI 10.4310/ACTA.2026.v236.n2.a2 (the DOI comes from a search summary; I could not read the journal front matter). The 36Kr report (9 Feb 2026) says it was accepted after nearly three years of review; the BICMR news page (dated 30 Jul 2026) announces online publication.
events.revisions: v2 6 Aug 2023 (retitled, per abstract page). Acta Mathematica 236 (2026), 365–416 (search summary). Publication date in the journal is not established by a readable source.
events.delivers: Geometric (function-field, characteristic 0) Bombieri–Lang for hyperbolic projective X with a finite morphism to an abelian variety. The abstract as read states the argument is conditional on the non-degeneracy conjecture for partial heights. The 2026 survey by Xie says that conjecture is proved in this paper for varieties finite over abelian varieties. Not the number-field statement.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the arithmetic statement over number fields and its extensions, the surface case, and the refined and strong forms. Geometric cases outside the hyperbolic finite-cover class are also not covered.

checked_by.qualification: journal of record for the published version
checked_by.what_they_did: accepted the paper after roughly three years of review, per the 36Kr report

checked_by.qualification: arithmetic geometers working on Parshin's method and related Bombieri–Lang questions
checked_by.what_they_did: wrote an expository survey explaining Parshin's proof and an alternative route to a Xie–Yuan case; see event bartsch-javanpeykar-2024

events.time_since_posted: about 3 years from arXiv v1 (May 2023) to the 2026 journal publication reported by BICMR
events.doubts: The abstract as read makes the approach conditional on the non-degeneracy conjecture for partial heights. A search summary of Bartsch–Javanpeykar says the link between partial height and standard height is not known in general, and the 2026 survey says the conjecture is proved only for varieties finite over abelian varieties. The 36Kr report calls it a conjecture the proof relies on. No specific error has been identified.
events.direction: Proves the geometric analogue for the stated class, in the direction the conjecture predicts (finiteness / non-density for the function-field version). Not a claim about number fields.

events.what_happened: Junyi Xie and Xinyi Yuan, 'The Geometric Bombieri-Lang Conjecture for Ramified Covers of Abelian Varieties', arXiv:2308.08117 (first submitted 16 Aug 2023; one version listed). Abstract as read: proves the geometric Bombieri–Lang conjecture for projective varieties with finite morphisms to abelian varieties of trivial trace over function fields of characteristic 0, using entire curves and an explicit description via Lie algebras of abelian varieties. The page says it was split from arXiv:2305.14789 v1.
events.revisions: One version listed on the abstract page read.
events.delivers: Geometric (function-field, characteristic 0) Bombieri–Lang for projective varieties finite over an abelian variety of trivial trace. The abstract as read states no conditional hypothesis. Not the number-field statement.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. Also the non-trivial-trace finite-cover case, which Gao's 2025 claim is said to address.
events.time_since_posted: about 3 years; no independent engagement found in searches. The 2026 survey by Xie cites a Xie–Yuan ramified-covers paper under a key name, but I could not confirm that key maps to this arXiv number.
events.direction: Proves the geometric analogue for the trivial-trace finite-cover class, in the direction the conjecture predicts. Not a claim about number fields.

events.what_happened: Finn Bartsch and Ariyan Javanpeykar, 'Parshin's method and the geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture', arXiv:2407.10706, submitted 15 Jul 2024, v2 24 Oct 2024. A short survey. It explains Parshin's proof of the geometric Bombieri–Lang conjecture and argues that Parshin's method gives an alternative proof of Xie–Yuan's result for projective varieties with empty special locus admitting a finite morphism to a traceless abelian variety. No new theorem is claimed.
events.revisions: v2 24 Oct 2024 (from the arXiv page read).
events.delivers: Expository. Re-derives a restricted geometric (function-field) case by Parshin's method. Adds no case beyond the Xie–Yuan class and says nothing about number fields.

checked_by.qualification: arithmetic geometers; Javanpeykar's work is on Bombieri–Lang and Campana-type questions (per search summaries)
checked_by.what_they_did: digested Parshin's proof and checked that it yields an alternative route to a Xie–Yuan case

events.time_since_posted: about 2 years 3 months as of 11 Oct 2026
events.direction: No change in direction. Consistent with Xie–Yuan's geometric result.

events.what_happened: Guoquan Gao, 'A complete proof of the geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture for ramified covers of abelian varieties', arXiv:2511.17010 v1 (21 Nov 2025; comment 'comments welcome!'). Abstract as read in v1: proves the geometric Bombieri–Lang conjecture for projective varieties with finite maps to abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0; generalises Xie–Yuan, which needed either the hyperbolicity or the non-isotriviality assumption; the proof 'is based on their strategy for constructing entire curves, but requires some new ingredients from algebraic geometry and Nevanlinna theory'. Revised v2 (2 Mar 2026) is retitled 'A counting argument for the geometric Bombieri-Lang conjecture on ramified covers of abelian varieties'. Its comment says 'We changed the title and the structure of the article, particularly in Section 1 and 3; we also fixed some typos'. The v2 abstract says the proof 'hinges crucially on a new counting argument'. The statement is the same in both versions. The 2026 survey by Junyi Xie cites this preprint as [Gao26] and presents the result as completed. BICMR (30 Jul 2026) describes it as proving the conjecture 'for all finite ramified covers of abelian varieties'. No journal publication or referee report was found.
events.revisions: v1 21 Nov 2025 ('A complete proof of…'). v2 2 Mar 2026 ('A counting argument for…'); comment says title and structure of Sections 1 and 3 changed and typos fixed. No later version listed on the abstract page read.
events.delivers: Claims, unconditionally per the v1 and v2 abstracts, the geometric (function-field, characteristic 0) Bombieri–Lang for projective X with a finite morphism to an abelian variety, dropping Xie–Yuan's hyperbolicity and non-isotriviality hypotheses. Stated over function fields only, and says nothing about number fields.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. No arithmetic statement over number fields or their finitely generated extensions is addressed.

checked_by.qualification: co-author of the Xie–Yuan results the paper extends; the v2 acknowledgements name Junyi Xie and Xinyi Yuan as Gao's advisors
checked_by.what_they_did: 2026 survey states that Xie–Yuan and Gao together prove the geometric conjecture for varieties with finite morphisms to abelian varieties, and that 'Gao completed the general finite-cover case by a new counting argument'. The survey describes the argument; it does not report a verification.

events.time_since_posted: about 11 months since v1 (21 Nov 2025) and about 7 months since v2 (2 Mar 2026) as of 11 Oct 2026
events.doubts: (1) v1 was titled and framed as 'A complete proof'; v2 was retitled 'A counting argument' and the abstract describes the new ingredient differently. The sources read give no reason for the change. (2) No journal acceptance, referee report, or independent expert check was found in searches on zbMATH-type sources, MathOverflow, and withdrawal or erratum terms. (3) The endorsements found come from the author's advisors (Xie and Yuan, per v2 acknowledgements; BICMR calls Gao their student) and from the 2026 survey by Xie, so they are not independent. (4) A summarising read of v2 Section 1 reports that Remark 1.6 says the proof depends on an unproven conjecture in the reduction steps of Section 4, 'especially the Green–Griffiths–Lang conjecture for finite covers of abelian varieties'. I could not verify this in the full text, and it would make the claim conditional on an open conjecture if correct.
events.direction: Claims the geometric analogue, in the direction the conjecture predicts (finiteness / non-density for the finite-cover class), over function fields. It is not a claim about the number-field statement the bullet names.

events.what_happened: Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Jerson Caro, 'A refined Chabauty–Coleman bound for surfaces', arXiv:2501.03483 (first submitted 7 Jan 2025; v2 3 Feb 2025). Refines the Caro–Pasten explicit bound on the rational points of a hyperbolic surface embedded in an abelian variety of rank at most one, applied to W2 := C + C for a hyperelliptic genus-3 curve C over Q. Combined with work of Siksek, it determines W2(Q) in a selection of examples.
events.delivers: An explicit refined bound and the determination of W2(Q) for selected genus-3 hyperelliptic curves over Q. A single family over Q. Finiteness of rational points on subvarieties of abelian varieties is already known (Faltings, per the Wikipedia article read), so this is effective determination, not a new finiteness theorem. The abstract does not say whether W2 is of general type.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: no general statement for surfaces of general type over number fields; only the computed examples.
events.time_since_posted: about 1 year 9 months as of 11 Oct 2026. I did not search for citing work, so 'none found' means none found in my searches, not verified absent.
events.direction: Explicit determination for specific surfaces over Q. Consistent with the finiteness the conjecture predicts, though that finiteness is already known for this type of subvariety.

events.what_happened: Junyi Xie, 'Recent progress on the geometric Bombieri–Lang conjecture', arXiv:2607.02165 (ID is for July 2026; the PDF metadata gives 3 Jul 2026). A survey by a single author. It says Xie–Yuan and Gao together prove the geometric conjecture for varieties admitting finite morphisms to abelian varieties. It states that for finite covers of abelian varieties the expected arithmetic (Bombieri–Lang) statement 'is still open', and that the conjecture 'remains very open in higher dimension'. It presents Gao's counting argument as completed. It claims no new theorem. The acknowledgements thank 'the AI assistant Xiaozhua for assistance during the writing process' and 'for providing the AI-agent environment and for resolving related technical issues'. One read attributed the AI environment to Liang Xiao and Shuai Chen; the second read did not show those names.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the arXiv ID read.
events.delivers: Restates the geometric result (Xie–Yuan plus Gao) for finite covers of abelian varieties. No new mathematics.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The survey says the number-field statement remains open.

checked_by.qualification: co-author of the Xie–Yuan results and advisor of Gao, the paper it reports as complete
checked_by.what_they_did: surveys Gao's counting argument as completed; gives no independent verification

events.doubts: The author is a co-author of the prior results and Gao's advisor, so the survey's account of Gao's argument is not an independent reading.
events.direction: Reports the geometric finite-cover case as proved (Xie–Yuan and Gao) and the arithmetic statement as open.

events.what_happened: Finn Bartsch and Ariyan Javanpeykar, 'Weakly special varieties, Campana stacks, and Remarks on Orbifold Mordell', arXiv:2603.28745 (submitted 30 Mar 2026). Constructs the first weakly special surfaces that are not Campana-special, including the complement of x²y³ = 1 in A². Shows that non-density of O_{K,S}-integral points on that surface is equivalent to Campana's Orbifold Mordell conjecture for (G_m, ½[1]). The abstract does not mention Bombieri–Lang or rational points on surfaces of general type.
events.delivers: Concerns integral points and the weak-specialness and Campana conjectures on one surface. It does not address rational points on surfaces of general type over number fields.
events.time_since_posted: about 6 months as of 11 Oct 2026; citing work not searched
events.direction: Not about the bullet. A neighbouring Campana / orbifold Mordell result.
events.object: The complement of x²y³ = 1 in A² (the plane curve complement), a surface on which integral-point non-density is equivalent to Campana's Orbifold Mordell conjecture for (G_m, ½[1]). Explicit as a surface; the equivalence is a conditional statement, not a proof of non-density.

summary: The arithmetic statement named in the bullet (weak, refined and strong Bombieri–Lang over number fields and finitely generated extensions) appears unchanged since January 2024. Searches (30 queries, listed below) and reads of the Wikipedia article, the arXiv abstract pages for 2305.14789 v2, 2308.08117, 2511.17010 v1 and v2, 2407.10706, 2501.03483, 2603.28745 and 2012.15765, the HTML of the 2026 Xie survey (2607.02165) and of Gao v2 (2511.17010), the BICMR news page, and the 36Kr report found no new case of the arithmetic statement. The Wikipedia article's own account of known cases (Faltings for curves and for subvarieties of abelian varieties) is unchanged in what I read. The only post-January-2024 mathematical claim on this territory is Gao's geometric claim. I record it as an analogue, not a resolution of the bullet, because it is over function fields of characteristic 0 and the bullet names number fields. Its status: first posted as 'A complete proof' (21 Nov 2025); retitled 'A counting argument' (2 Mar 2026) with a comment that Sections 1 and 3 changed. Neither version's abstract names a gap, but the wording of the new ingredient changed. The author's advisors (Xie and Yuan) endorse it in the 2026 survey, which is not an independent reading. No journal acceptance, referee report, or verification by a non-collaborator was found. Also, a summarising read of v2 reports that Remark 1.6 makes the reductions in Section 4 depend on the Green–Griffiths–Lang conjecture for finite covers of abelian varieties; I could not confirm this in full text, and if it holds, the claim is conditional on an open conjecture. The Xie–Yuan results that Gao extends were first posted in 2023 (outside the window), are conditional in general on a non-degeneracy conjecture for partial heights (unconditional for varieties finite over abelian varieties, per the 2026 survey and the Bartsch–Javanpeykar survey as summarised in search), and were published in Acta Mathematica in 2026 (per the 36Kr report and the BICMR news page; the DOI comes from a search summary). AI: no source I read names an AI system in the mathematics of any event. The Gao v2 acknowledgements thank Xie, Yuan, She Yang, Jihao Liu, Ariyan Javanpeykar and the NSFC, with no AI mention, though I could not read the full text reliably (see incomplete). The 2026 Xie survey acknowledges 'the AI assistant Xiaozhua for assistance during the writing process' and an 'AI-agent environment' for technical issues; these concern writing and set-up for a survey, not mathematics this problem depends on, so I did not record a system in ai.systems and set none_found false for that event. Whether the AI environment was used for Gao's paper is not stated. No model name is credited with any mathematics on this problem, so no release-date lookup is needed. Neighbouring AI items seen in search and not recorded as events for this bullet: an arXiv preprint (2609.15930) on GPT-assisted proofs of the Cassels–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for cubic surfaces (search snippet only, not opened); OpenAI's May 2026 disproof of Erdős's unit-distance conjecture (a different problem, search snippet only, not opened). Conditional applications of Bombieri–Lang (Shaffaf 2018, Ascher–Braune–Turchet 2020, Tao's 2019 blog on polynomial bijections, Erdős–Ulam 212) are pre-window and conditional; they were seen in snippets, not opened. None of them moves the problem.
competing_reading: Read 'Bombieri–Lang conjectures' in the plural with 'field extensions' broadly, so that a function field such as C(B) counts as a field extension. Then the geometric results of Xie–Yuan (2023, Acta 2026) and Gao (2025) are cases of the bullet's own content: a class of varieties (projective, finite over an abelian variety, characteristic 0) would be settled for the geometric form of the conjecture, and the Gao claim would be a case-level resolution. On that reading, the whole of Gao's extension counts, and the event's AI record is none. Against it: the bullet names number fields, the geometric conjecture is a separately named version, and the Gao claim is unrefereed with a changed title and a possible conditional dependency in Section 4. The narrower reading gives no new result in the window.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Journal acceptance of arXiv:2511.17010, or a written check of its counting argument by a specialist outside Xie and Yuan's circle, including whether Section 4 relies on the Green–Griffiths–Lang conjecture for finite covers of abelian varieties. (2) The reason for the v1-to-v2 retitling and whether any step of v1 was withdrawn. (3) A full-text read of Gao v2 and of the Xie–Yuan papers for AI disclosures, since my reads of them were abstract- or summary-level. (4) A scope ruling on whether 'field extensions' in the bullet includes function fields over C. (5) For the arithmetic statement, any new case over a number field; none was found.

incomplete: (1) Gao 2511.17010: the PDF returned compressed bytes, so I could not read the full v2 text. The HTML was read in two chunks by a summarising fetch, and the two reads disagree about where the acknowledgements sit and how far the text runs. So the AI check for Gao's paper covers what I read (acknowledgements, Section 1, and parts of Section 3) and does not cover the complete text or the reference list. The claim about Remark 1.6 and the Green–Griffiths–Lang dependence comes from one summarised read and is unverified. (2) Acta Mathematica front matter: unreadable, so the DOI, volume and page numbers come from a search summary and the 2026 publication date from the BICMR and 36Kr pages only. (3) Xie–Yuan 2305.14789 and 2308.08117: abstract pages only; the AI check is at abstract level. (4) Bartsch–Javanpeykar 2407.10706 and 2603.28745, Balakrishnan–Caro 2501.03483: abstract pages only. (5) The Xie survey 2607.02165 HTML was read in two chunks; the acknowledgements and references were read, the final 8,219 characters were not. The survey's AI environment attribution (Liang Xiao and Shuai Chen) appeared in one read and not the other. (6) BICMR GBL_RC.pdf redirected and was not followed.
